narration.text: Why 3.5 million people fled the Great Plains.
In the 1930s, dust storms blackened the sky.
About 400,000 square kilometres of farmland were hit.
Drought met ploughed soil with no grass to hold it.
In just over a year, over 86,000 people reached California.
Modern farming practices now protect much of that soil.
So the Dust Bowl was drought plus human choices.
